source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "ដំណាំល្ហុង" (Papaya Cultivation), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
As the papaya tree grows, the source recommends applying fertilizer starting around one month after transplanting, then continuing on a regular schedule as the tree develops toward flowering and fruiting. Water the trees roughly twice a week, adjusting for rainfall so the soil around the base stays moist without becoming waterlogged.

Once the tree begins to flower and set fruit, remove excess or malformed flowers/young fruit and any unwanted side growth so the plant channels its energy into producing well-shaped, good-quality fruit rather than an overcrowded, uneven fruit set.
caveat: The source's exact fertilizer type/dosage schedule beyond 'around one month after transplanting' was not fully legible; only the general timing and watering frequency are stated with confidence.
